prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe for percentage coupons the rearrangement inequality says pair the largest discount with the largest price; with minimum-spend coupons, sweep items cheapest first, releasing each coupon whose minimum the item meets into a max-heap, and take the largest available. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: **Reconstructed — only the title was reported.** You buy items with prices `prices[i]` and hold coupons `percentOff[j]`. Each coupon takes that percentage off **one** item; each item takes **at most one** coupon. Return the **minimum total** you pay.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can coupons stack on one item? (No.)
- Must every coupon be used? (No.)
- Percentage or flat amounts? (Stage 1 percentage; stage 2 flat with a minimum spend.)
- Money type? (decimal, no rounding.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A discount is worth the most on the most expensive item, so sort both and pair them. Once coupons have minimum prices, a coupon only fits items above its minimum — so process items cheapest first and, for each, use the best coupon it qualifies for; expensive items will still qualify for anything the cheap ones could.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "F."or percentage coupons the rearrangement inequality says pair the largest discount with the largest price; with minimum-spend coupons, sweep items cheapest first, releasing each coupon whose minimum the item meets into a max-heap, and take the largest available."

learn.title: 5 · Why the approach works

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe for percentage coupons the rearrangement inequality says pair the largest discount with the largest price; with minimum-spend coupons, sweep items cheapest first, releasing each coupon whose minimum the item meets into a max-heap, and take the largest available. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call MinTotalFlat concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Using double for money.
- Greedy from the most expensive item with the biggest eligible coupon — it can waste a coupon only a cheaper item could use.
- Applying a coupon to an item below its minimum.
- O(n·m) matching instead of a heap.
